#### 1. early-onset progressive encephalopathy-hearing loss-pons hypoplasia-brain atrophy syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.476)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8876198)

**Proposed mechanism:** TRAPPC11 (HGNC:24234) —DISRUPTS→ Endoplasmic Reticulum-Golgi trafficking (GO:0006888); TRAPPC12 (HGNC:24235) —DISRUPTS→ Endoplasmic Reticulum-Golgi trafficking (GO:0006888); Endoplasmic Reticulum-Golgi trafficking (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ Progressive encephalopathy (HP:0002370); Endoplasmic Reticulum-Golgi trafficking (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ Hearing loss (HP:0000365); Endoplasmic Reticulum-Golgi trafficking (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ Pons hypoplasia (HP:0011670); Endoplasmic Reticulum-Golgi trafficking (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ Brain atrophy (HP:0002079). Mutations in TRAPPC11 and TRAPPC12 disrupt the TRAPP complex, impairing ER-Golgi trafficking. This dysfunction leads to progressive encephalopathy, hearing loss, pons hypoplasia, and brain atrophy in both disease entities.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in TRAPPC11 or TRAPPC12 with a gnomAD allele frequency greater than 0.1% in any population. _(variant: Any pathogenic variant in TRAPPC11 or TRAPPC12)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TRAPPC11 and TRAPPC12 in ER-Golgi trafficking could lead to therapeutic strategies that target this pathway for both diseases.

Impaired ER-Golgi transport leads to a cascade of cellular dysfunctions manifesting as progressive encephalopathy, developmental delay, seizures, and episodic rhabdomyolysis.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with loss-of-function variants in TRAPPC11 or TRAPPC2L who do not present with any of the core phenotypes of either MONDO:0014144 or MONDO:0032681, or the presence of common, high-frequency pathogenic variants in gnomAD for the causal genes associated with these specific diseases. _(variant: Exome allele frequency > 0.01 for variants in TRAPPC11 or TRAPPC2L in relevant populations.)_
